The government is quietly paying you up to seven hundred and eighty-nine ringgit a month. Here's the catch.
Meet two drivers. A Myvi, and a giant SUV. Both pay one ringgit ninety-nine a litre.
But the real price this week? About four ringgit sixty. The government pays the rest.
The Myvi fills up forty litres. The SUV? Eighty. So every full tank, the SUV gets double the subsidy.
In 2022, fifty-three sen of every subsidy ringgit went to the richest twenty percent. The poorest forty got just fifteen.
The bill this year? Up to forty billion ringgit.
That's why BUDI ninety-five caps it at three hundred litres a month.
But scrap it completely, and transport, food, everything gets pricier.
So, keep it, or cut it? Comment below, and follow The Common Cents.
